builds.howItPlays: You pay Jayce's Empower cost once to unlock his upgraded ability, which lets you ready two pieces of gear at once instead of one, so your best Equipment and gadgets fire twice in the same turn. You spend your early turns setting up gear and reserves so that once Jayce is empowered, one turn can do the work of two.
builds.whyYou: You like a deck that rewards patience early and pays it back with a turn where everything suddenly clicks into place. You're comfortable holding back and setting pieces up rather than swinging every turn, and you enjoy the moment when a well-timed activation gets you two effects for one. Jayce suits you if you want to be the player quietly setting pieces up before turning them loose all at once.
builds.ratingNotes: Ability: Empower cost 2 energy + 2 rainbow runes, use only if not Empowered; 1 energy + Exhaust: ready a gear; once Empowered, 1 energy + Exhaust: ready 2 gear (Riftcodex, VEN). pace 3.5: riftbound.gg describes the deck operating 'at a deliberate pace, using ramp and draw to set up its core strategy' before it pays off. stance 5: riftbound.gg calls it 'primarily proactive' but notes it keeps 'a bit of early control to keep the opponent in check,' so it splits between setting its own plan and holding back answers. complexity 7.5: riftboundguide calls it a 'high-skill-ceiling' deck where 'you must decide when to spend' the Empower cost since it determines whether you ready one gear or two, and riftbound.gg separately calls the sequencing 'moderate-to-high.' variance 6: riftboundguide says the deck has 'significant swing potential once Empowered, allowing exhausted Gears to activate twice in one turn,' on top of only 'moderate' baseline consistency. archetype Combo: riftboundguide names it directly, 'Gear combo decks reward players who like sequencing and setup over straightforward aggression,' and the two-gear Empower payoff reads as a real combo turn rather than a steady unit plan. Domain note: one fetched summary claimed the deck runs 'Mind-only' runes, which conflicts with the card's confirmed Mind/Body domains (Riftcodex) and the other source's framing of Jayce as 'the first ever Body-Mind legend'; treated as a fetch summarization error and ignored. This Legend's mind-body coordinate is 0 by design per the brief, since Mind and Body cancel out on that Axis. Confidence: medium, two guides read and they agree on the deck's shape, but neither gives a full tournament-level decklist breakdown, and the domain discrepancy above is worth a reviewer's second look. starterDeck kept null: no guide names a confirmed retail starter product for this specific printing; one search turned up an unconfirmed note that Jayce's own Champion Deck had not gone on sale separately as of these sources.
